name: seccomp_unotify
synopsis: int seccomp(unsigned int operation, unsigned int flags, void *args);
int ioctl(int fd, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_RECV, struct seccomp_notif *req);
int ioctl(int fd, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_SEND, struct seccomp_notif_resp *resp);
int ioctl(int fd, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD, struct seccomp_notif_addfd *addfd);
description: The seccomp user-space notification mechanism allows a seccomp filter to delegate system call handling to another process. It uses ioctls to receive notifications and send responses. This is not intended for implementing security policy.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: Operation to perform, such as SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Pointer to arguments for the operation

return_value.success: Returns 0 on success for seccomp and ioctls
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, errno is set

errors.description: Target thread terminated or system call interrupted
Notification already responded to or not fetched

bugs: This mechanism is explicitly not intended for implementing security policy; it may have limitations in retrieving pointer arguments due to race conditions.
examples: int fd, removeFd; fd = openat(req->data.args[0], path, req->data.args[2], req->data.args[3]); struct seccomp_notif_addfd addfd; addfd.id = req->id; addfd.srcfd = fd; addfd.newfd = 0; addfd.flags = 0; addfd.newfd_flags = O_CLOEXEC; targetFd = ioctl(notifyFd, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD, &addfd); close(fd); struct seccomp_notif_resp *resp; resp->id = req->id; resp->error = 0; resp->val = targetFd; resp->flags = 0; ioctl(notifyFd, SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_SEND, resp);
